title: `theme.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor` shows incorrect color and changing appearance when it includes an alpha value
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Although including transparency in theme colors isn't recommended, the dataframe headers are incorrect to a greater extreme than some overlapping color: The header initially appears almost black and then changes to the designated colors (sans transparency) as you hover over it.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37dd4ce9-ac02-4a55-88eb-0b7355a2e317

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.dataframe({"A": [1, 2, 3], "B": [4, 5, 6]}, on_select="rerun")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

```
#config.toml
[theme]
dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor = "#FF00001a"
```
1. Run the app.
2. Move the cursor on and off the header to see the color change.

### Expected Behavior

The header color should be consistent. Some slightly different colors from overlapping transparent layers might be expected, but not a drastic color shift from almost black.

### Current Behavior

The color shifts from near black to the equivalent color without the alpha layer in the header of the dataframe (as you hover-unhover repeatedly).

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.46.2.dev20250714
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: Mac
- Browser: Prisma


### Additional Information

_No response_

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-11950)

Note: changes to the configuration option seems to be more dependent on restarting the session to reflect the change, which may be due the complexity of the dataframe. I wonder if there is a common underlying issue here. Although we may not want to invest in supporting transparency exactly, we should still want a good developer experience where theming configuration changes reflect without needing reboots or new sessions.
